chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Saeed, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:

It is disliked to cut the palm tree. And he was asked about cutting the tree, so he said: 'There is no problem.' I said, 'So what about the lote tree (sidr)?' He said: 'There is no problem with it. Rather, it is disliked to cut the lote tree in the wilderness because it is scarce there, and as for here, then it is not disliked.'

key_terms.مَكْرُوهٌ: Disliked (a legal ruling between permissible and forbidden)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on cutting palm trees and other trees in the wilderness versus inhabited areas?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between general environmental stewardship and specific ecological preservation, ruling that cutting palm trees is generally disliked (makruh) due to their economic and agricultural value. He clarifies that the prohibition against cutting the lote tree (sidr) is context-dependent, applying primarily to the wilderness where scarcity makes them vital for shade and resources, while permitting their removal in inhabited areas. This nuanced ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on *maslaha* (public interest) and the balance between human utility and preserving natural ecosystems.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Ahmad Bin Al Hassan, from Amro Bin Saeed, from Musaddaq Bin Sadaqa, from Ammar Bin Musa, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘It is abhorrent, cutting the palm tree’.

And he<sup>asws</sup> was asked about cutting the tree. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem’. I said, ‘So (what about) the lote tree?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with it. But rather it is disliked to cut the lote tree in the wilderness because these are scarce with it, and as for over here, so it is not disliked’.
en.sarwar: 8. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Ahmad ibn al-Hassan from ‘Amr ibn Sa‘id from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from ‘Ammar ibn Musa who has narrated the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

cutting down of palm trees is detestable. He (the Imam) was asked about cutting down of trees. He (the Imam) replied, ‘It is not unlawful.’ I then asked about cutting down of lotus trees. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not unlawful. It is detestable to cut them down in the wilderness because it is very rare there, however, here it is plentiful.’”
